title: [Technical] Establish repeatable CI and release-quality baseline
body:
## Objective
Make the current Expo SDK 57 baseline reproducible before remote services are added.

## Scope
- Commit and enforce `package-lock.json` with `npm ci`.
- Run dependency check, Expo Doctor, lint, typecheck, and checkout guards in CI.
- Add smoke-test evidence for all drawer routes and the direct-vote flow.
- Define supported Android/iOS versions and test large text and short screens.

## Acceptance criteria
- A clean clone passes all checks using the pinned Node/npm toolchain.
- CI fails on dependency drift or an uncommitted lockfile change.
- Manual smoke-test evidence is attached.

## Out of scope
Backend connectivity and product data.

title: [Technical] Audit and harden the Supabase migration baseline
body:
## Objective
Validate and harden the single squashed pre-production Supabase baseline before any remote integration.

## Scope
- Apply `202610120001_baseline.sql` from zero in disposable local Supabase.
- Review table purpose, constraints, UTC boundaries, invoker security, grants, revocations, and default privileges.
- Verify RLS on every exposed table and run the pgTAP access tests.
- Add tests for zero votes, ties, duplicate votes, disabled questions, finalization, and missing records.
- Confirm no shared or production database consumed the discarded prototype migrations.

## Acceptance criteria
- Local reset, database tests, and database lint succeed from an empty database.
- Automated tests prove active results cannot leak and finalized votes cannot mutate.
- Remote dry-run contains only the baseline migration and the fresh-project strategy is approved.

## Depends on
T01.

title: [Technical] Add Supabase read-only health connectivity
body:
## Objective
Prove safe mobile-to-Supabase connectivity before reading or writing product data.

## Scope
- Add the current compatible Supabase JavaScript client.
- Configure `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and the publishable key only.
- Add typed configuration validation and a harmless health endpoint/query.
- Render missing-config, connecting, success, and failure states.

## Security constraints
Never embed a secret/service-role key, database password, FCM credential, or translation API key.

## Acceptance criteria
- Android and iOS development builds connect successfully.
- Missing or invalid configuration fails clearly.
- Bundle inspection finds no server secrets.

## Depends on
T02.

title: [Technical] Replace the hardcoded Today question with a read-only query
body:
## Objective
Load the active UTC daily question from Supabase without enabling voting writes.

## Scope
- Add a typed API module, TanStack Query provider, and `useTodayQuestion` hook.
- Implement loading, empty, error, retry, and cached-last-known states.
- Validate UTC rollover and refresh behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- Updating the active question in Supabase updates the app without rebuilding.
- No vote mutation is introduced.
- Date rollover tests pass.

## Depends on
T03.

title: [Technical] Connect paginated finalized Past Results with caching
body:
## Objective
Replace preview records with all public finalized questions.

## Scope
- Add one paginated result summary endpoint/query; avoid N+1 card requests.
- Return question, asked date, finalization time, YES/NO percentages, result, and vote count.
- Add pagination, pull-to-refresh, errors, empty state, and persisted cache.
- Join personal vote markers locally; do not expose personal history through the public RPC.

## Acceptance criteria
- Active/unfinalized results never appear.
- Results are available regardless of participation.
- Previously loaded pages remain readable offline.

## Depends on
T04.

title: [Technical] Implement an idempotent secure vote write path
body:
## Objective
Accept one immutable server-confirmed vote per installation and question.

## Scope
- Use a secured Edge Function or RPC to validate question status, UTC window, and YES/NO input.
- Issue and verify an installation credential; do not trust arbitrary client device IDs or fingerprints.
- Enforce uniqueness, rate limits, and idempotency/replay handling server-side.
- Derive network abuse signals server-side and return an immutable vote receipt ID.

## Acceptance criteria
- Duplicate, late, malformed, and replayed requests are rejected deterministically.
- A retry returns the original accepted receipt rather than adding a vote.
- The UI records only server-confirmed votes.

## Depends on
T04 and T02.

title: [Technical] Add durable local cache and offline behavior
body:
## Objective
Allow offline browsing without compromising vote integrity.

## Scope
- Monitor connectivity and show a non-blocking offline state.
- Persist finalized-result pages and server-confirmed vote receipts.
- Disable voting offline with clear copy.
- Never queue a vote for later upload.

## Acceptance criteria
- Airplane mode can browse previously downloaded results/history.
- Offline voting cannot appear accepted.
- Cache migration and corruption recovery are tested.

## Depends on
T05 and T06.

title: [Technical] Add optional email account and canonical history merge
body:
## Objective
Let users preserve answered-question history across devices without making signup mandatory.

## Scope
- Add verified email OTP/magic-link authentication; names remain optional.
- Link the authenticated account using `auth.uid()`, never a client-supplied account ID.
- Claim server-known installation votes transactionally and idempotently.
- Preserve the established account vote on duplicate-question conflicts.
- Add account-only history RLS, audit records, logout cache cleanup, and deletion/anonymization flow.

## Acceptance criteria
- Device A history restores on Device B after verified login.
- Retried/interrupted merges do not duplicate or overwrite votes.
- Anonymous use remains fully functional.

## Depends on
T06 and T07.

title: [Technical] Implement tested My Pulse calculations
body:
## Objective
Replace the placeholder with trustworthy personal agreement insights.

## Scope
- Calculate answered count, agreement/disagreement counts and percentages from canonical history and finalized results.
- Require at least 10 eligible finalized answers.
- Define ties explicitly; recommended: exclude ties from agreement denominator and show them separately.
- Add unit tests for 0, 9, 10+, ties, missing results, and merged histories.

## Acceptance criteria
- Metrics are deterministic and explainable.
- No insight appears before the threshold.
- UI clearly states denominator and tie behavior.

## Depends on
T08 and T05.

title: [Technical] Brewing: one submission and one upvote per UTC day
body:
# T10 — One daily Brewing submission and one daily upvote per verified account

This updates the previous weekly-submission proposal: the approved limit is now **one submission per UTC day** and **one upvote total per UTC day**, on another user's question.

## Requirement and implementation

- Everyone can browse; a signed-in, email-verified account is required to submit/upvote.
- Limits reset at 00:00 UTC, independent of device timezone, cache, reinstall or local clock.
- Enforce unique account/day records in PostgreSQL under concurrent requests. Reject self-upvotes server-side; exact retries do not consume a second action.
- Only dedicated RPCs may write. Do not accept author/voter IDs or quota dates from clients. Do not expose author IDs/emails in the public feed.
- Provide input validation, paginated question list, counts, own/upvoted indicators, server allowance loading/error states, and explicit midnight reset copy.
- All open submissions remain browsable and eligible across days. At 00:00 UTC, accumulated pre-boundary upvotes select the live question without administrator schedule overrides. Equal totals prefer the later submission, then UUID. Hidden/selected questions are excluded. Moderation now hides open candidates with a required reason and immutable private audit; notification delivery remains separate work.

## Owner rollout

1. Merge/pull the implementation PR and inspect pending migrations with `npx supabase db push --dry-run` in the checkout linked to hosted DEVELOPMENT.
2. Apply migrations with `npx supabase db push`. Do not reset existing votes/results.
3. Ensure Supabase email OTP authentication is enabled with the project's email provider and correct app deep-link/redirect settings. Verify real account sign-in on both platforms; no phone/name is required by this feature.
4. Rebuild/install Android preview and, when available, the signed iOS build. For Expo Go/development clients, restart Metro/reload JavaScript.
5. Test with two verified accounts: first submission succeeds, second distinct submission is rejected, one upvote succeeds, another different upvote is rejected, self-upvote is rejected. Restart/clear app data and sign back in: allowances must remain used.
6. Test 00:00 UTC reset, different device timezones, retries/concurrency, offline attempts, unverified accounts and anonymous browsing. Offline writes must not be queued.
7. Review open submissions and the automatic selection result. Only the community ranking decides the winner; old scheduled dates cannot reserve or override it. Test ties and multi-day upvote totals. Test audited moderator confirmation/cancel and rejected stale/revoked access.

## Done criteria

Automated database/client tests and physical-device evidence cover limits, self-vote rejection, unverified/guest rejection, idempotence, concurrency, privacy, and UTC reset. Role-management UI and announcements remain separate milestones. See docs/brewing-community-rules.md for the current implementation and role bootstrap.

title: [Technical] Introduce server-side translation workflow incrementally
body:
## Objective
Translate questions without exposing provider keys or paying two providers by default.

## Scope
- Start with one server-side provider, preserve original text, cache by question/language/version, and support admin correction.
- Capture quality and cost metrics.
- Run a measured comparison before adding a second provider or automated evaluator.

## Acceptance criteria
- No translation key appears in the mobile bundle.
- Original language is always viewable.
- Failed translation falls back safely.
- A documented experiment determines whether dual providers are justified.

## Depends on
T10.

title: [Technical] Add FCM HTTP v1 daily notification delivery
body:
## Objective
Notify opted-in users when the daily question goes live at 00:00 UTC.

## Scope
- Add permission UX and server-side token registration/rotation/removal.
- Send through FCM HTTP v1 using service-account OAuth, never a legacy server key.
- Schedule at 00:00 UTC and monitor delivery failures/invalid tokens.
- Deep-link into Today and support opt-out.

## Acceptance criteria
- Test devices receive one notification per daily publication.
- Invalid tokens are retired.
- Credentials remain server-side.
- Delivery is observable and retry-safe.

## Depends on
T06; do not launch until the core daily loop is reliable.

title: [Feature] Show total vote count with every finalized result
body:
## User outcome
A result shows not only percentages but how many accepted votes produced it.

## Requirements
- Display a localized count such as `128,421 votes` on result detail/cards where space permits.
- Count only accepted votes included at finalization.
- Define zero-vote and tie presentation.
- Do not imply statistical representativeness; label the population as PULSE voters.

## Acceptance criteria
- Count matches the finalized server aggregate.
- Large counts use locale-aware formatting.
- Accessibility reads result, percentages, and count coherently.

## Depends on
T05.

title: [Research] Define minimum sample and reliability rule for any future country result
body:
## Decision needed
What minimum evidence is required before showing a country-level split?

## Constraints
Country reporting is deferred and must not be inferred from phone code, locale, SIM, or IP. A future implementation requires optional self-declared country, privacy review, anti-switching controls, and honest “PULSE voters in X” labels.

## Research scope
- Choose a minimum sample threshold and whether it varies with margin of error.
- Define copy: `Not enough votes for a reliable country result.`
- Suppress percentages and winner below threshold.
- Evaluate small-cohort privacy and manipulation risk.
- Require sample size and unweighted-sample disclosure above threshold.

## Acceptance criteria
A written product/statistical/privacy decision is approved before country data or UI is implemented.

## Out of scope
Implementing country collection now.

title: [Feature] Gate yesterday’s landing-page reveal while keeping Past Results public
body:
## User outcome
A returning voter sees yesterday’s result on Today; a non-voter gets warm, non-punitive copy directing them to Past Results, where all finalized questions remain public.

## Copy direction
Avoid guilt or false assumptions such as “you were busy.” Recommended tone: `We missed your voice yesterday. Explore the result in Past Results.`

## Rules
- Landing-page reveal checks canonical/local participation for yesterday’s question.
- Non-voters do not receive the inline reveal, but can open the same public result in Past Results.
- Account/device changes must not incorrectly hide a known account vote after sync.
- Accessibility and deep links must still reach Past Results.

## Acceptance criteria
Voter and non-voter paths are tested, including logged-out, restored-account, missing-cache, and offline states.

## Depends on
T05, T07, and eventually T08 for cross-device accuracy.

title: [Feature] Show result publication countdown in the device timezone
body:
## User outcome
Everyday UI shows a server-derived countdown and the canonical absolute UTC deadline: `Results in 6 hours and 12 minutes — tomorrow at 00:00 UTC (21 Oct 2026)`. Any optional local-time display must remain secondary to the explicit 00:00 UTC boundary.

## Requirements
- Treat 00:00 UTC as the canonical server boundary.
- Derive display from a server timestamp, not a hardcoded 24-hour client timer.
- Use device locale/timezone and handle DST, timezone changes, clock skew, backgrounding, and minute rollover.
- An information screen may explain that the global question changes daily at 00:00 UTC.

## Acceptance criteria
Tests cover UTC± offsets, half-hour/quarter-hour zones, DST transitions, device timezone changes, and a stale client clock.

## Depends on
T04.

title: [Feature] Implement the post-vote counted receipt and live countdown
body:
## User outcome
After server acceptance, show:

`Vote counted`  
`You voted YES`  
`Results in 18h 41m`  
`Come back when tomorrow’s question goes live.`

## Requirements
- Show only after the server returns an accepted immutable receipt.
- Use the canonical publication timestamp and the shared localized countdown component.
- Persist the receipt across restarts.
- Distinguish pending, rejected, duplicate/idempotent success, and accepted states.

## Acceptance criteria
The receipt survives restart, never appears for a rejected/offline vote, and remains accessible at large text sizes.

## Depends on
T06, T07, and F04.

title: [Feature] Notify a submitter when their question is selected
body:
## User outcome
A submitter can opt to learn that their question was selected for the daily Pulse.

## Identity decision
A device signature is not a communication channel and is not durable after reinstall. Use:
- push notification to an opted-in installation token for anonymous users; and/or
- verified email for users who voluntarily link an account.
Do not require email merely to submit a question.

## Requirements
- Store submission ownership as installation identity plus optional account ID—not raw email on the submission.
- Record a durable `selected` event and send each configured channel idempotently.
- Define behavior after reinstall, logout, token rotation, account merge, duplicate marking, veto, and selection reversal.
- Keep notification preferences and unsubscribe controls.

## Acceptance criteria
The submitter receives at most one notification per selection event through opted-in channels; no device fingerprint is treated as an address.

## Depends on
T10, T12, and optionally T08.

title: [Technical] One active signed-in device and complete login/logout lifecycle
body:
# One active signed-in device: complete login/logout journey

Specification only; do not implement or enable enforcement in the language/preferences change. Extend the existing authentication/session-lifecycle issue (T13) instead of duplicating it.

Requirement: a successful sign-in on device B replaces account access on device A. Public browsing remains available after A is signed out. Daily/community limits, existing votes and saved preferences remain attached to the account.

Implementation plan:

1. Represent the active authenticated session with a server-owned account session generation/lease, bound to the verified Supabase session ID and device session. Atomically claim it only after successful email-code verification, including simultaneous logins. Failed/abandoned login attempts must not eject the existing device. Never accept a client-supplied user ID as authorization.
2. Revoke replaced refresh sessions using supported Supabase administration APIs. JWT expiry/refresh-token revocation alone does not invalidate an already issued access token immediately: check the active generation at every authenticated data/action boundary (RPC/Edge/admin). Keep credentials server-side. Evaluate Supabase plan/session controls rather than assuming an unavailable feature is enabled.
3. A private per-account Realtime invalidation channel/sign-out event makes an online foreground device react promptly. Validate on startup, foreground, reconnect and before private writes; use bounded polling as a recovery path. Server enforcement takes effect with the session replacement transaction. An offline/suspended device cannot receive an immediate UI logout: discard its session and private UI at its first reachable validation. State this limitation clearly.
4. Clear old auth tokens, private queries, nickname/account caches and subscriptions on logout/replacement. Preserve chosen local appearance, public content and already accepted vote protections. A late response from old account A must not reappear in account B's UI.
5. Show “You signed in on another device. Sign in again to use your account here.” Give a clear guest continuation. Explicit logout applies only to the current session; a stale device cannot revoke a newer session. Lost-device recovery/account deletion must revoke the authoritative active lease too.

User journey and acceptance tests on Android and iOS:

- New/existing users: same email → code flow, no account enumeration, invalid/expired/delayed/resend/rate-limit errors, retry after lost network. Only verified successful login claims the lease.
- A signed in → B signs in → A's private operations fail immediately, online A becomes guest promptly, B restores theme/language. Public browsing remains usable.
- A offline or background → B signs in → A resumes/reconnects and clears private data before any private request succeeds; no promise of push delivery to a disconnected app.
- Simultaneous A/B login, stolen/replayed refresh token, stale JWT, reconnect after long sleep, device clock tampering, notification loss, repeated account switching, logout during in-flight request, app reinstall/storage clear and server outage.
- One successful generation wins races; old session cannot mutate profile/preferences/read status/community votes/moderation or remove the new session. Existing database vote uniqueness still applies.

Owner setup: confirm Supabase plan/auth settings and production email provider, supply Android and signed iOS devices for cross-device testing, agree offline/recovery copy. No Apple signing change is needed to design the server policy; physical iOS acceptance follows signing readiness.

title: [Feature] Complete optional-account entry points and honest completion UX
body:
## User outcome
Users can discover optional accounts in context without distracting from today's vote.

## Scope
- Keep account management inside Settings; do not add another top-level drawer destination.
- Maintain prompts in My Pulse, Past Results, Brewing Questions, and after a server-confirmed vote.
- Return users to the initiating context after verification.
- After T08, show server-confirmed merge progress and counts; never claim local data is protected before confirmation.
- Keep anonymous reading and voting fully functional.

## Acceptance criteria
- Prompts disappear while authenticated and never block core actions.
- Account completion distinguishes verified email, local nickname, and server-confirmed merged records.
- Copy remains accurate before and after history sync is released.

## Depends on
T08 and T13.

Updated rule: daily voting remains usable without sign-in; community submission/upvote actions require a verified account.

title: [Feature] Add privacy-safe nickname attribution to shares and selected questions
body:
## User outcome
A user may add a device-local nickname to a specific share or selected community question without exposing an internal identifier.

## Rules
- Default share credit is `My PULSE · <date>` with no identifier.
- Nickname attribution is explicit opt-in for every share; do not remember consent globally.
- Default selected-question credit is `Community question`; public nickname credit is separate per-question consent.
- Never expose device IDs, installation credentials, auth UUIDs, email addresses, push tokens, or fingerprints.
- Because nickname is device-only, it must be re-entered after device change and removed locally at logout.

## Acceptance criteria
- Snapshot/export tests prove prohibited identifiers cannot render.
- Removing a nickname immediately removes it from future previews.
- Moderation, Unicode/confusable, impersonation, length, and accessibility behavior are approved before public question credit.

## Depends on
The real share pipeline, T10, and the moderation decision.

title: [Research] Threat-model device eligibility and duplicate voting across devices
body:
## Decision needed
Define enforceable device eligibility, session behavior, and duplicate-vote policy without implying that a device equals a human.

## Stress-test scenarios
- The same email signs in on two physical devices before either session refreshes.
- One person uses several physical devices, reinstalls, clears storage, restores backups, or clones app data.
- One person uses a different verified email on every device.
- Devices are shared, lost, offline, or transferred while a vote is in flight.
- Account history and installation history contain conflicting votes for one question.

## Critical constraints
The product rule is one accepted vote per eligible physical device and question. Supabase single-session enforcement does not establish device identity. Installation secrets do not survive every reinstall. Platform attestation can reject many scripts/emulators but is not a permanent cross-platform device ID. Device fingerprints are mutable, spoofable, and privacy-invasive.

## Research scope
- Model abuse economics, false positives, accessibility/shared-device harm, offline races, recovery, reinstall, and transfer.
- Evaluate App Attest, DeviceCheck, Play Integrity, device recall, request binding, rate limits, risk scoring, verified accounts, and sampling.
- Specify transactional conflict policy and auditable idempotency.
- Decide whether strict reinstall prevention requires verified accounts where platform recall cannot supply a stable guarantee.

## Acceptance criteria
An approved threat model, exact public product claim, data-flow/privacy review, platform support matrix, conflict matrix, and abuse-response plan exist before enforcement.

## Out of scope
Treating CAPTCHA, email, a local secret, or a client-generated identifier as proof of a physical device.

title: [Research] Design secure anonymous Pulse transfer with a QR handoff
body:
## User outcome
A non-account user can intentionally transfer eligible local/server-known Pulse history to a new device.

## Security requirements
- Never encode a raw device ID, installation secret, email, auth token, or history payload in the QR code.
- Prefer a server-issued, one-time, short-lived, audience-bound transfer challenge.
- Require confirmation on the old device, authenticated claim on the new installation, replay protection, expiry, cancellation, and credential rotation.
- Define whether the old installation is revoked, retained read-only, or can recover after an interrupted transfer.
- Define conflict handling, lost/broken old device behavior, screenshots of QR codes, clock skew, offline states, and support/audit controls.

## Acceptance criteria
A reviewed protocol and abuse/privacy model demonstrates atomic transfer, no replay, no secret disclosure, and deterministic recovery.

## Out of scope
Implementation before T06/T07 installation credentials and receipts exist.

title: [Legal/Product] Complete global youth safety, age-rating, and launch-country review
body:
## Decision needed
Define where and for whom PULSE can legally and safely launch.

## Ruthless premise check
App Store/Play age ratings and parental controls are distribution aids, not a transfer of the developer's legal duties. `No adult content` does not eliminate child-privacy, consent, profiling, notification, UGC/moderation, retention, deletion, advertising, dark-pattern, or local-content risks. Adult questions may also change ratings and country availability.

## Scope
- Obtain qualified counsel and build a country-by-country launch matrix for age thresholds, parental consent, data rights, and restricted topics.
- Decide age assurance/minimum-age UX without collecting unnecessary sensitive data.
- Define question/submission moderation, escalation, reporting, crisis topics, election/health claims, and emergency takedown.
- Complete store questionnaires/ratings, privacy disclosures, retention/deletion/export policy, notification consent, analytics/ads decision, and incident response.
- Test youth-comprehensible copy, accessibility, coercion/dark-pattern risk, and parental-control behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
Legal/product/security sign-off exists for each launch country, unsupported regions are blocked appropriately, and policies/operations are live before youth marketing.

## Out of scope
Assuming stores alone enforce every country's law.

title: [Security] Complete global launch abuse and operations gate
body:
## Objective
Take the gateway-only vote path from a secure baseline to a globally operated service.

## Scope
- Validate App Attest and Play Integrity server-side with privacy review; voting must fail closed when required verdicts are unavailable or invalid.
- Add gateway/IP/ASN risk controls without storing raw network identifiers longer than necessary.
- Add dashboards, alerts, kill-switch drills, secret rotation, load/penetration tests, runbooks, and rollback exercises.
- Publish an honest unweighted PULSE-participant methodology; state the one-eligible-physical-device rule and its measured reinstall limitations precisely.

## Acceptance criteria
Independent security review, capacity test, incident drill, privacy sign-off, and launch SLOs pass.

## Note
The repository now has a gateway, database kill switch, hashed installation credentials, and bounded per-installation attempts. Attestation and production operations require external platform/infrastructure configuration and remain open.

title: [Technical] Validate and operate atomic daily finalization
body:
## Objective
Operate the idempotent 00:00 UTC finalization/publication transaction safely.

## Scope
- Test zero votes, ties, delayed/duplicate runs, missing next question, concurrent invocation, and rollback.
- Alert on schedule drift, multiple/no live question, and finalization failure.
- Add an authorized manual replay procedure and immutable audit evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
A staging soak test crosses multiple UTC boundaries without leaks, duplicate snapshots, or downtime.

## Note
The database function and pg_cron schedule are implemented; deployment validation and monitoring remain open.

title: [Technical] Complete canonical account-history lifecycle
body:
## Objective
Turn transactional installation-history claims into a complete privacy-safe account lifecycle.

## Scope
- Surface sync status/counts and canonical history in the app.
- Test conflicting device/account votes and interrupted/retried merges.
- Implement export, deletion/anonymization, retention, logout cache clearing, and support audit tooling.
- Ensure account deletion does not mutate finalized aggregate snapshots.

## Acceptance criteria
Cross-device restore, deterministic conflict handling, deletion/export, and privacy tests pass.

## Note
Idempotent claim and account-history RPCs are implemented; lifecycle UX and data-rights operations remain open.

title: [Security] Enforce physical-device voting and best-effort reinstall resistance
body:
Status: planned; Android ID/IDFV, receipt recovery and database uniqueness are intermediate controls, not attestation. This issue extends the existing T17 requirement rather than creating another competing security policy.

## Work the coding agent can implement

1. Verify the maintained Expo/native integrity module against this repository's Expo SDK, then add native configuration and a Play-internal EAS profile. Expo Go cannot provide this verification.
2. Issue short-lived, single-use server challenges bound to the complete vote payload, account/install identity and idempotency key. Persist consumption/replay state transactionally; never trust client success flags.
3. Android: obtain a Standard integrity token with the request hash; decode on the server using Google-authorized credentials. Check package, allowed Play signing certificate, PLAY_RECOGNIZED, LICENSED, MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY, binding and freshness. Reject unsupported form factors and invalid verdicts.
4. iOS: register an App Attest key using attestation, then use assertions. Validate the official Apple trust chain, app identity, environment, challenge, signature and increasing counter. Persist key association, revocation and replay state. Verify using trusted public Apple roots; an Apple API private key is not needed solely to verify App Attest. DeviceCheck, if separately adopted, has different API credentials.
5. Keep vote/account/fingerprint uniqueness and CAPTCHA. Add quota/outage handling, privacy-safe telemetry, automated malformed/replayed/wrong-app tests, physical-device tests and reviewed production rollout controls. Do not silently bypass attestation in production.
6. Add developer diagnostics that distinguish wrong signing, Play licensing, unsupported device, quota and provider outages without logging tokens. Use observe-only staging before reviewed enforcement; production fail-closed protects writes while reads remain available.

## Android owner steps (do these in your accounts)

1. Create/confirm a Google Play Console developer account and an app with this exact package: com.pulse.worldtoday. Confirm ownership of the package before changing identifiers.
2. In Google Cloud Console create/select a dedicated project. In Play Console > app > App integrity > Play Integrity, link that Cloud project following Google's setup flow. Enable the Play Integrity API in the linked project if prompted. Record the project number (non-secret).
3. Configure Play App Signing. Record the SHA-256 fingerprint of the **app signing certificate**, not merely the upload key/EAS local signing certificate. The server must allow the certificate installed by Play. Coordinate signing-key rotation rather than replacing allowed digests blindly.
4. Create the server identity authorized to call the Play Integrity decode API in the linked project, with least-privilege permissions. Use a supported server workload identity or, if a JSON service-account key is necessary for the deployment, enter it through secure Supabase configuration after the agent provides the exact secret binding. Never paste keys in chat, Expo public variables or Git.
5. Once the native implementation is ready, use a Play-internal EAS profile that extends preview but sets distribution=store, environment=preview and android.buildType=app-bundle. The agent will supply that profile with the integration PR. Build with `npx eas-cli@latest build --platform android --profile play-internal`.
6. Upload the AAB to Play Console > Testing > Internal testing. Add tester Google accounts and publish the internal release. Each tester must accept the opt-in link and install from Play using the enrolled account. A sideloaded preview APK does not establish the intended licensing/recognition path.
7. Provide the project number, package and signing certificate fingerprint to the agent; these are non-secret. Run physical-device canaries, then test modified builds, wrong signing, replay, offline/provider outages and data clearing. Approve enforcement only after reviewing false rejections and accessibility/support impact.

## iOS owner steps (after Apple enrollment)

1. Enroll in Apple Developer, confirm the Team ID and register com.pulse.worldtoday under the intended team.
2. Enable the App Attest capability for the identifier/provisioning setup as required by Apple's current tooling. Let the agent add the matching entitlement/config plugin; regenerate provisioning profiles after entitlement changes.
3. Register physical tester iPhones for internal development distribution or configure TestFlight for store distribution. App Attest is not a simulator/Expo Go verification path.
4. Use EAS signing with the intended team and the integration's build profile, then install that signed build on supported physical iPhones. The entitlement environment, signed application identity and server expectations must agree; do not mix development and production attestations.
5. Share only Team ID/bundle ID and non-secret diagnostics. App Attest verification itself needs trusted public roots and app configuration; do not create or send a .p8 key for it. If optional DeviceCheck is later added, configure its separate credentials securely at that stage.
6. Run registration, assertion, replay, counter, app-data clearing, reinstall, key-loss, unsupported-device and outage tests. After staging review, enable the approved production policy.

## Acceptance and limitations

- Genuine approved physical-device builds can vote; replay, payload substitution, forged app identity and unverifiable verdicts cannot authorize writes.
- Tests prove the complete client/server binding and denial paths, with privacy-safe operations evidence.
- Neither platform supplies a general permanent device identifier or unlimited reinstall-persistent per-question history. DeviceCheck/device recall are optional additional signals, not a guarantee or sole launch dependency. Keep database uniqueness and be explicit about residual limits.
- No one-human-one-vote claim. Requiring durable identity for daily voting is a separate product decision; verified account is already required for community submissions/upvotes.

Official setup references:
- https://developer.android.com/google/play/integrity/setup
- https://developer.android.com/google/play/integrity/standard
- https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/establishing-your-app-s-integrity

title: [Security] Complete native Turnstile CAPTCHA step-up for voting
body:
## Objective
Production-harden the implemented native Turnstile vote challenge without treating CAPTCHA as device identity.

## Implemented foundation
- A tightly scoped Supabase Edge Function serves the widget with restrictive CSP and no-store headers.
- The Expo app renders it in an allowlisted React Native WebView with cancellation, loading, and failure UX.
- The token is bound through cData to credential, question, choice, and idempotency key; the gateway recomputes that binding.
- Siteverify fails closed and requires exact `pulse-vote` action, configured hostname, and cData. Tokens are submitted only with the pending vote.

## Remaining external and hardening work
- Configure separate test/staging/production widgets, exact hostnames, sitekeys, secrets, rotation, quotas, and privacy disclosure.
- Add a gateway risk-decision/challenge endpoint so low-risk voters need not always be challenged.
- Add a server-issued, single-use, short-lived nonce to the existing payload binding and persist nonce consumption.
- Complete physical-device accessibility, alternative-path, expiry/background, provider-outage, replay, payload-substitution, and false-positive testing.
- Monitor Turnstile analytics and Siteverify rejection reasons without logging tokens or identifiers.

## Acceptance criteria
Replayed, expired, wrong-action, wrong-hostname, wrong-cData, malformed, and provider-rejected tokens fail closed; production secrets stay server-only; accessibility and staged false-positive reviews pass; platform attestation remains mandatory.

## Depends on
T17, provider configuration, and T19.

title: [Research] Evaluate device + verified email + verified phone voting
body:
## Product direction
Move PULSE closer to **one person, one vote** after anonymous device voting has proven adoption and after a measured, reviewed rollout. Perfect proof of personhood is not promised. The goal is to make duplicate voting materially harder by requiring all three independent controls: a server-recognized eligible device, a verified email address, and a verified phone number.

## Proposed identity and voting invariants
- A login succeeds only after separate, short-lived OTPs sent to both the normalized email address and normalized E.164 phone number are verified in the same server transaction.
- One verified phone can bind to only one verified email, and one verified email can bind to only one verified phone. The resulting immutable internal `person_identity_id`—not either raw value—is the voting identity.
- A persistent session may vote daily without repeating both OTPs. New sign-in, account recovery, sensitive identity changes, or risk escalation requires both factors again.
- Vote acceptance requires a currently valid identity session **and** the eligible-device controls from T17.
- The database enforces one accepted vote per question for both `person_identity_id` and recognized device. Application checks are not sufficient.
- Email/phone changes require re-verification, a cooling-off period, notification to both old channels where possible, session revocation, abuse review, and auditable recovery.

## Required scenarios
1. **Normal login:** the user enters both OTPs. The email/phone pair becomes exclusive. Once the session is established, the user can vote daily without recurring OTP friction until logout, expiry, revocation, recovery, or risk escalation.
2. **Same device, different identity pair:** after the device votes, logout followed by a different verified email/phone pair cannot create another vote for that question because device uniqueness has already been consumed.
3. **Same identity pair, different device:** after the identity votes, login on another eligible device cannot create another vote for that question because identity uniqueness has already been consumed. The second device may participate on later questions subject to policy.
4. **Concurrent race:** simultaneous requests from multiple devices for the same identity, or multiple identities from the same device, result in exactly one accepted vote through database uniqueness and transactional locking.
5. **Reinstall/reset:** device recall/fingerprint/attestation controls reconnect the device where supported; identity uniqueness still blocks a second vote after login when device recall is unavailable.
6. **Dual-SIM/multiple-email attacker:** different legitimate pairs and different physical devices may bypass the model. Measure this residual risk; do not claim it is eliminated.
7. **Shared/recycled phone:** family/shared numbers, reassigned numbers, lost access, SIM swap, number porting, and deceased/inactive owners require explicit recovery and dispute rules without silently transferring voting history.
8. **Aliases and normalization:** email aliases/case rules, Gmail-style plus addressing, internationalized domains, E.164 normalization, VoIP/temporary numbers, carrier changes, and country-code ambiguity must have deterministic policy. Do not implement provider-specific alias collapsing casually.
9. **Account lifecycle:** test logout, session theft, refresh-token replay, lost device, remote session revocation, email-only loss, phone-only loss, deletion, export, legal hold, and re-registration after deletion.
10. **Availability and inclusion:** test SMS/email delay or outage, travel/roaming, sanctioned or unsupported regions, users without SMS service, accessibility, minors, and support escalation. No silent fallback may weaken both-factor verification.

## Ruthless premise check
The combination will substantially raise the cost of casual duplicate voting, but it still does not prove one natural person. A motivated actor can obtain several devices, SIMs, and emails; SIM farms and synthetic identities exist. Conversely, one-phone-per-email can exclude families, schools, refugees, travelers, low-income users, and users of recycled numbers. The assumption that bypassers are a small percentage must be tested with evidence rather than embedded as a security premise. Download count or traffic alone is not an adequate rollout trigger.

## Research and rollout scope
- Define measurable abuse, integrity, participation, exclusion, support-cost, and geographic-bias thresholds that justify collecting phone numbers.
- Compare this proposal with passkeys, platform attestation/device recall, carrier intelligence, account reputation, privacy-preserving proof-of-personhood, and transparent device-based sampling.
- Complete threat modelling, DPIA/privacy review, telecom/vendor review, country launch matrix, retention/deletion policy, breach response, and qualified legal review.
- Prototype in an isolated environment, then run opt-in and observe-only experiments before staged enforcement. Keep an immediate rollback path.
- Decide whether raw email/phone values remain solely with authentication vendors; application tables should prefer opaque identity IDs and minimum derived metadata.
- Publish methodology as **one verified identity-and-device vote**, not one-human-one-vote, unless a separately reviewed proof-of-personhood system justifies that stronger claim.

## Acceptance criteria
- Database and concurrency tests prove one accepted vote per question across both recognized device and `person_identity_id`.
- Both OTPs are required for every new authentication ceremony and sensitive identity change; sessions are securely persisted, revocable, and risk-step-up capable.
- All scenarios above have approved outcomes, recovery rules, user copy, telemetry, privacy controls, and abuse/support runbooks.
- A measured pilot shows material fraud reduction with acceptable participation loss, accessibility, geographic bias, false rejection, cost, and support burden.
- Security, privacy, legal, product, and operations owners approve staged rollout and public claims.

## Do not implement yet
Keep the current anonymous/device phase until R01, R03, T14, T16, T17, and T19 are operationally proven and this research gate passes. Do not collect phone numbers merely because PULSE crosses an arbitrary download or traffic threshold.

title: [Operations] Deploy monitoring, alerts, and recurring incident drills
body:
## Objective
Turn the repository monitoring primitives and runbook into continuously verified production operations.

## Implemented foundation
- Privacy-safe structured vote gateway events with request IDs and bounded reason/status fields.
- Authenticated `operational-health` Edge Function backed by a service-only aggregate health RPC.
- Optional critical alert webhook delivery and a repository readiness guard.
- Incident response runbook covering kill switch, secret compromise, CAPTCHA outage, alert delivery, finalizer replay, and rollback.

## Remaining external work
- Configure a Supabase log drain, dashboards, retention/access controls, primary and backup alert destinations, and an external uptime caller in every environment.
- Set SLOs and tested thresholds for absence of health checks, latency/errors, rejection anomalies, question cardinality, scheduler/finalization lag, and alert-delivery failure.
- Execute quarterly drills and retain evidence; remediate every failed objective by an owned deadline.
- Add independent load and penetration tests and verify the monitoring pipeline during those tests.

## Acceptance criteria
Production and staging generate actionable alerts to two destinations, a synthetic check detects whole-project failure, on-call ownership is documented, and every required drill has recent evidence with detection/recovery times. No sensitive identifier or token enters logs or alerts.

## Depends on
T14, T15, production Supabase deployment, and an approved monitoring provider.

title: [Feature] Ten app languages and synced theme/language preferences
body:
# Language settings, account preferences, and stored content translations

Update the existing internationalization issue if one exists; do not duplicate the question-translation issue. Link the two issues with the `question-translation` label (create that label if absent).

Requested languages, as explicitly chosen by the owner: English (`en`), Mandarin Chinese (`zh-Hans`, simplified script initially), Hindi (`hi`), Spanish (`es`), Modern Standard Arabic (`ar`), French (`fr`), Bengali (`bn`), Portuguese (`pt`), Russian (`ru`), Urdu (`ur`). This is the owner's launch selection, not a claim that these are the ten largest individual languages by native speakers. Regional/script variants can follow.

Implemented in this change:

- Settings language selector with native language names; immediate static UI, navigation, accessibility labels, dates, numbers and countdown language changes. Arabic/Urdu use right-to-left text and layout. Vote values and stored content are never translated by dictionary substitution.
- Guest theme/language stored in SQLite on the current app installation. Clearing app storage removes guest settings; a different device starts with defaults. Current appearance remains after logout.
- Account language/theme saved in `user_preferences` through owner-checked, authenticated RPCs; restored at sign-in on another device. New-device defaults never replace existing account settings. Pending offline edits retry on reconnect/foreground and update only edited fields. The same-field last successful write wins; multi-device session exclusion is a separate issue.
- Existing device theme migrates forward. Whitelisted values, strict owner validation, no public preference-table access, per-project/account pending cache, explicit sync status/retry.
- Today/final results request the selected content language. Missing stored question translations fall back to original text, without disguising fallback as translated content.

Remaining content translation requirement (link T11 / existing AI-question issue):

- Keep original question, detected source language, immutable source revision and human correction provenance. Translate using one server-side AI provider into all supported languages, persist reviewed/selected versions in `question_translations`; never translate on every app read. No provider key in app builds.
- Community submissions can use any language. Automatically promoted submissions currently carry `source_language='und'` until source-language detection/content translation is implemented. An app-language preference is not proof of the language someone typed.
- Announcements use the same supported locale policy but a separate revisioned content table/workflow. Publishing requires complete translations or an explicit visible original-language fallback policy.
- Human linguistic review, Android/iOS large-text and screen-reader testing, RTL checks, mixed-script content, localized email templates/CAPTCHA provider language and regional variants remain release checks. Provider-generated diagnostics are not guaranteed to be localized by the static UI catalog.

Acceptance: all static message catalogs have matching keys and interpolation placeholders; switching language does not change question IDs, vote choices or receipt identity. Guest restart, sign-out, account switch, cross-device restore, offline edit/restart/reconnect, stale responses and independent-field updates pass. Static-string internationalization and AI-generated question translation have separate acceptance and deployment status.

title: [Feature] Multilingual in-app announcement center
body:
# Multilingual in-app announcements for guests and accounts

Design/specification only. Do not implement the app, announcement database, publisher or jobs in the language/preferences change. This is separate from FCM/APNs push notification delivery (T12): checking on open/foreground and manual refresh is sufficient.

Recommended UX:

- Home top-right bell, accessible label and generous touch target. A small green dot signals new items; include an accessible “new announcements” state, not color alone.
- Tapping opens a full-height screen sliding from the right. This better accommodates translated paragraphs, large text, small devices, safe areas, screen readers and pagination than a small dropdown. Show heading, close/back, refresh top-right, scrollable list, loading/empty/offline/error states, and last successful refresh. Keep existing list visible during refresh; prevent duplicate refresh requests.
- Tap a list item to show detail as a sheet/modal above the list. Closing it restores the list's scroll position, filters and refreshed items. Android Back closes detail first, list second. Screen-reader focus enters detail and returns to its list item. External links are explicit and allowlisted, never executed from arbitrary announcement markup.
- Signed-in accounts: unread rows have stronger emphasis, read rows muted but fully interactive. Detail offers explicit **Mark as read** or **Mark as unread**, with the current status explained; either saves then closes. On failure show retry and keep the detail open; do not falsely report saved status. Merely opening a detail does not override the explicit choice. Read states follow the account across devices and survive reinstall/sign-in.
- Guests: neutral rows without read/unread controls. Detail has **Okay**. A device-local last-seen feed revision drives only the bell dot, not per-item read state. Mark the captured list revision seen when the list opens; announcements arriving later retain the dot. On reinstall/new device, guests see current announcements as new.
- Optional dropdown alternative must support outside-tap dismiss only when no detail is open, preserve the dropdown behind detail, trap/restore focus correctly, and expand to full-screen for large text. Prefer one full-screen behavior for the initial release. See the editable SVG mockup in `docs/design/announcements-proposal.svg`.

Delivery and storage:

- Superuser-only draft/publish/withdraw. Original text + source language + immutable source version; server-side AI translations stored per locale/version. No translation API call or secret in a client read. Review/completeness gate before publication. A newer source version invalidates old translation readiness; users must not see mismatched translation versions. An explicitly missing locale shows a labelled original-language fallback.
- Published/scheduled/expired/withdrawn lifecycle, starts_at/ends_at in UTC. Serve only authorized live content. Expired/withdrawn/deleted content must disappear from caches. A scheduled future announcement must not leak through a public feed before release.
- Do **not** send every cached timestamp. Use a bounded delta endpoint with opaque cursor encoding feed epoch, committed revision and locale. Return changes (versioned upserts/tombstones), next cursor, pinned committed high-water revision, server_time, nearest transition, and whether a full snapshot is required. Limit pages (for example 100) and payload size; deduplicate by announcement ID and apply only increasing per-item revisions.
- Critical: a plain sequence/nextval is allocation-ordered, not commit-ordered. Transaction A can allocate 100, B commit 101, client checkpoint 101, then A commits 100 and is lost. Use a transactional counter locked through commit for this small broadcast feed, or an equivalent change stream with a proven committed checkpoint. A cursor must never jump an uncommitted gap. Add an index on committed revision and retain tombstones/change records for the offline window.
- Initial consistent snapshot pins a watermark, pages live content, then catches changes after that watermark. Apply pages and advance cursor atomically in the device store; failures/retries must not lose events. Respect expired cursors/changed feed epochs with explicit snapshot reset; never return a misleading empty delta. Translation-language changes reset the language-scoped snapshot rather than reusing another locale's body.
- Publication, translation correction, withdrawal, activation and expiry create lifecycle revisions. Check visibility against server time on every response; return the next transition for a client timer. Foreground and bounded TTL/manual refresh recover missed activation jobs. Do not rely on an expiry write/event alone to stop showing expired content. Avoid timer dependence on an untrusted device clock.
- Cache public announcement content by project/locale/feed epoch. Store read state separately by authenticated account with indexed `(user_id, announcement_id)` and owner-checked RPCs/RLS. Track the last acknowledged content revision too: a substantive newly published revision becomes unread again, while a translation-only correction follows an explicit policy. Server changes to read state have their own version/checkpoint; public content cursor alone cannot synchronize read/unread across devices. Versioned updates resolve races deterministically, with idempotent retries; never replay account A's pending mark under account B.
- On app startup/foreground fetch a bounded delta, deduplicate in-flight pulls, use ETag/304 where appropriate, backoff + jitter on failures, retain valid cached content, and use a bounded retry interval while the screen is open. No permanent per-guest server identity is necessary. No background polling promise while the OS suspends the app.

Design-model stress validation:

Run `node docs/design/announcement-sync-model.mjs`. The deterministic local simulation processed 100,001 committed changes with page size 100, duplicate delivery, stale replay, concurrent arrivals while paging, equal timestamps, allocation-vs-commit ordering, cursor retention/epoch reset, locale scope, account read isolation and scheduled visibility/expiry. Final cached content matched the server model. For 10,000 known notices, a JSON timestamp list was 558,891 bytes versus 60 bytes of cursor metadata (responses excluded). Local run was about 0.1 seconds; this is neither a hosted load test nor a production latency target.

Future acceptance/load tests: real PostgreSQL transactional counter and aborted transactions, simultaneous publishers/readers, large payloads and translated text, rollout fan-out and CDN hit rate, snapshot consistency, log compaction, 30+ day offline devices, clock drift, missing translations, screen-reader/RTL/large-font behavior, read-state races between devices, logout/revocation during save, account switches, airplane mode and repeated refresh. Define latency/error/retention/payload budgets before implementation. Preserve immutable audit history and server-owned role checks. Link language, admin/superuser and single-device-session issues.


Detailed interpretation and limits of the 100,001-change model are documented in docs/design/announcement-sync-explained.md. This remains a design experiment, not deployed announcement infrastructure.

title: [Feature] Server-enforced admin moderation and superuser publishing
body:
# Server-enforced admin and superuser roles

Implemented foundation: server-owned private admin/superuser roles, own-role RPC, open-candidate removal modal/RPC, required reason and append-only private audit. Role-management UI, announcement publishing, restoration, last-superuser recovery and single-session enforcement remain specifications only. See `docs/brewing-community-rules.md` for trusted SQL role bootstrap and tests.

Roles (neither privileged role may nominate, schedule or override the next daily winner):

- Regular signed-in user: existing verified-account submission/upvote privileges only.
- Admin: regular-user functions plus removal of inappropriate community questions from public view.
- Superuser: admin functions plus assigning/removing admins and drafting/publishing/withdrawing announcements for everyone. Announcements are translated server-side using AI into the supported languages and stored before publication; users fetch them on open/foreground or refresh. No real-time delivery requirement.

Server/security requirements:

- Keep roles in a protected server-owned table. Every privileged operation verifies current authenticated identity, active session and current role in the database/service. Never trust client flags or editable user metadata; hiding a button is not authorization.
- Bootstrap the first superuser through a documented trusted SQL/admin operation using the verified auth UUID. Never ship a shared superuser password or a service key in the app. Recommend step-up/MFA for privileged users, with recovery defined before enforcement.
- Superuser may manage admins; promotion to superuser requires a separately controlled bootstrap/recovery operation. Prevent removal/deletion of the last superuser, concurrent role-change races and self-escalation. Role removals take effect at the next server operation, irrespective of stale UI/JWT metadata.
- “Remove question” means audited hide/moderation, with actor, reason, timestamp and question snapshot. A restoration/review UI and moderation rate limits remain follow-up work. Hidden submissions cannot receive votes or win selection. Preserve accepted votes and published immutable results; moderation of an already-live/historical question needs an explicit disclosure/redaction policy, not silent vote deletion.
- Announcement lifecycle: draft → translate → review → scheduled/live → expired/withdrawn, locale completeness/version checks, deterministic published revisions, safe plain text or sanitized markup, no arbitrary script/URL execution, audit log, retry-safe jobs and provider-cost limits. Role revocation cannot leave an unauthorized queued publication able to bypass current policy.

Acceptance: direct anonymous/regular/admin requests cannot assign roles or publish announcements; concurrent last-superuser protections hold; revoked admins fail even with cached UI. Test hide-vs-upvote/selection races, restoration, invalid translations, failed publication, scheduled expiry, account deletion and audit access on Android/iOS. Link the language, announcement-center and single-device-session issues.
